knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The range is the largest value minus the smallest: 4.5 minus 1.5 equals 3.0 hours. Option 1 is the IQR in the worked example, and option 2 is a value that does not follow from the data.

With an IQR of 0.75 and an upper quartile of 2.5, the line is 3.625 hours. Only the 4.5-hour job sits above it. The median is not flagged by this rule, and the rule does not flag jobs for being short.
A flagged job needs a cause before any standard or price changes. Deleting it hides real conditions, and charging every future job at the flagged time ignores whether the cause will recur.

practicalCriteria: Given at least nine job times or invoice totals for one service type, the learner calculates the range and the IQR correctly, showing the sorted list and both quartiles.
The learner applies the upper-line rule correctly and flags the right value or values.
For each flagged value, the learner records a cause and states whether it should change a standard time, a quote or nothing.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Worksheet with sorted values, range, quartiles, IQR and the flag line
Outlier notes for each flagged job with the cause and the decided action
Assessor observation of the learner explaining why a flagged job was or was not treated as a standard change
stopWorkCriteria: Stop and do not change a standard time or quote on the basis of one flagged job until its cause has been recorded.
Stop if the time unit in the records is unclear, such as minutes and hours mixed in one field, until the units are confirmed.
